items.prompt: Black's bishop on g6 is attacked. Tap every square it can legally move to (a capture counts).

claims.statement: The bishop on g6 can move to exactly these squares.

hints: The bishop moves along two diagonals through g6.
One diagonal runs toward c2, the other toward h5 and f7.
Count both diagonals: h7 and f5 on one side, h5 and f7 on the other, then e4, d3 and c2 beyond f5.
items.explain: A bishop moves along diagonals until something blocks it. From g6 the squares h7, f5, e4, d3 and c2 lie on one diagonal (the last is a capture of the c2 pawn), and h5 and f7 on the other. Nothing of Black's stands in the way.

items.prompt: White to move after 8...Bf7. How many black pieces defend the pawn on e6? (The king counts.)

claims.statement: Exactly one black piece, the bishop on f7, defends e6.

hints: Look at who stands next to e6.
Check the bishop's diagonals and the king's reach.
The bishop on f7 attacks e6; the king on e8 is two squares away and the queen on d8 does not see e6.
items.explain: The bishop on f7 stands next to e6 and defends it. The king on e8 is not adjacent to e6, and the queen on d8 sees d7 and e7 but not e6. So one defender: a single trade of attackers would leave e6 short.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's bishop on c4 points at e6. Choose the move that keeps Black ahead.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is the best reply.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nbd7 is at least 250 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...b5 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...g6 is at least 40 cp worse than the best move.

hints: One reply develops a piece and covers g4 and h5, the squares the white queen wants.
Think about which squares a white queen could use next, and which developing move covers them.
The knight from g8 reaches f6, where it covers g4 and h5.
items.explain: The knight on f6 develops, covers g4, h5 and d5, and leaves the b8 knight and the queen free. It does not touch e6, but it takes away the queen's best routes. Engine, depth 16: Black stays about half a pawn ahead. The natural-looking ...Nbd7 and ...b5 both lose the advantage at once.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: Nxf7 Kxf7 and now Qg4 attacks e6 twice; the knight on f6 would have covered g4. The engine rates it at least 250 cp worse.
feedback_by_move.b7b5: Bxe6 attacks the bishop on f7, and Nxf7 or Qh5+ follow. The engine rates it at least 400 cp worse.
feedback_by_move.g7g6: Safe-looking and playable, but it gives back the whole edge: the engine rates it about 40 cp worse than ...Nf6 or more.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...Nbd7. Black's knight attacks your knight on e5. Find the move that wins the advantage.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 10.Nxf7 is the best move.
Engine, depth 16: 10.Qg4 is at least 400 cp worse than the best move.

hints: Which of Black's pieces defends e6?
Take the defender of e6 with a capture that Black must answer.
The knight on e5 can capture the bishop on f7.
items.explain: The knight takes f7 and the king has to recapture, which removes the main defender of e6 and puts the king on f7. Next the queen arrives on g4 and e6 is attacked twice. Engine, depth 16: White is clearly ahead.

feedback_by_move.d1g4: Too early: the knight on d7 takes the knight on e5 and White has given a knight for a pawn. The engine rates 10.Qg4 at least 400 cp worse than 10.Nxf7.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...a6. If the queen goes to g4, is she attacked by a black piece?

claims.statement: After Qg4 no black piece attacks the queen.

hints: Count the black pieces that can reach g4.
Which black piece could attack g4, and is it still at home?
No black piece reaches g4: the g8 knight has not moved.
items.explain: After ...a6 nothing of Black's attacks g4: the knight is still on g8 and the pawn move does not touch the kingside. The queen route is open; whether it is good is a different question, answered by the board before.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...Nf6. If the queen goes to g4, is she attacked by a black piece?

claims.statement: After Qg4 the knight on f6 attacks the queen.

hints: Count the black pieces that can reach g4.
Check the knight on f6.
A knight on f6 attacks g4.
items.explain: The knight on f6 attacks g4 (and h5, d5, e4), so the queen would be attacked and could be captured. This is why the quiet reply works.

items.prompt: White to move after 9...b6. If the queen goes to g4, is she attacked by a black piece?

claims.statement: After Qg4 no black piece attacks the queen.

hints: Count the black pieces that can reach g4.
Check what the b-pawn move changed.
The pawn move on the b-file does not touch g4.
items.explain: The b-pawn move changes nothing on the kingside: still no black piece attacks g4. One difference matters (the knight on f6); the other (a pawn move on the queenside) does not.

items.prompt: Black to move. The pawn on g4 attacks your bishop on f5. Find a retreat that keeps the bishop safe and Black ahead.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Bh7 and ...Be4 are both within 60 cp of the best move.
After ...Be4 no white piece attacks the bishop on e4.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is at least 250 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...Qa5+ is at least 250 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The bishop is attacked by a pawn, so ignoring it costs a piece.
Two squares on the long diagonal are out of the pawn's reach.
h7 and e4 are both safe; a pawn on f3 could chase the bishop from e4.
items.explain: The bishop retreats along its diagonal to h7 or e4, out of the pawn's reach. Moves that ignore the attack, such as ...Nf6 or the check ...Qa5+, let White capture on f5 and win a piece. Engine, depth 16: both retreats keep Black clearly ahead, and the engine slightly prefers ...Bh7 (by roughly a tenth to four tenths of a pawn, depending on depth); ...Be4 can be chased by f3.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: The knight develops but ignores the attack: White takes the bishop on f5. The engine rates it at least 250 cp worse.
feedback_by_move.d8a5: The check gains a tempo but the bishop is still attacked: after the interposition White takes on f5. The engine rates it at least 250 cp worse.

items.prompt: White to move after 8...Bf5. Does a black piece defend the pawn on e6?

claims.statement: One black piece, the bishop on f5, defends e6.

hints: Look at the bishop's diagonals.
The bishop on f5 is next to e6.
f5 and e6 are neighbours on a diagonal.
items.explain: The bishop on f5 stands diagonally next to e6 and defends it. This is the guard White wants to deflect.

items.prompt: White to move after 8...Bh7. Does a black piece defend the pawn on e6?

claims.statement: No black piece defends e6 now.

hints: Look at the h7 bishop's diagonals.
The bishop on h7 looks along h7-b1 and h7-g8.
No black piece sees e6.
items.explain: The bishop on h7 looks at g6 and f5 (and g8), not at e6. The pawn on e6 stands alone: the c4 bishop will aim at it.

items.prompt: Black to move. The bishop on c4 attacks e6 and nothing defends it. Find a move that keeps Black clearly ahead.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Qd6 is the best reply and ...Nbd7 is within 60 cp of it.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...Qc8 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.

hints: The pawn on e6 is attacked and nobody guards it.
Which piece can guard e6 and also pressure the knight on e5?
The queen goes to d6; the b8 knight to d7 also helps.
items.explain: The queen on d6 guards e6 and attacks the knight on e5. The knight on d7 trades the intruder. Moves that develop elsewhere, such as ...Nf6, leave e6 hanging and White takes it with a strong attack. Engine, depth 16: both of the first two keep Black clearly ahead.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: Develops, but e6 is unguarded: White takes it. The engine rates it at least 150 cp worse.
feedback_by_move.d8c8: The queen retreats but still does not guard e6, and White takes it. The engine rates it at least 150 cp worse.

items.prompt: Black to move after 9.Bc4. White threatens g4 next. Find a reply that keeps Black clearly ahead.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...h5 and ...Qd6 are both within 60 cp of the top choice.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is at least 120 cp worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...g6 is at least 150 cp worse than the best move.

hints: White wants to chase the bishop with a pawn.
Either stop the pawn push or add a defender to e6.
...h5 stops g4; ...Qd6 guards e6 and hits the knight.
items.explain: The pawn on h5 prepares to answer g4 by capturing it, which opens the h-file for Black's rook [I]; the queen on d6 guards e6 and hits the knight on e5. Engine, depth 16: both keep Black clearly ahead. ...Nf6 lets g4 chase the bishop with tempo.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: Natural, but g4 now hits the bishop and the knight cannot help. The engine rates ...Nf6 at least 120 cp worse.
feedback_by_move.g7g6: Weakens f6 and h6 and lets g4 come with tempo. The engine rates it at least 150 cp worse.

items.prompt: White to move after 8...Bf7. Choose your development move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 9.Bc4 is the best move.

hints: Do not rush the queen.
Develop a piece that also points at a weak pawn.
The bishop from f1 reaches c4.
items.explain: The bishop develops and attacks e6, the pawn the f7 bishop has to guard. A queen raid to h5 loses the queen to the bishop on f7.

items.prompt: White to move after 8...Bf5. Choose a move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: 9.g4 is the best move.

hints: Is the bishop on f5 attacked by a pawn yet?
Which pawn can attack it?
The pawn on g2.
items.explain: The pawn attacks the bishop, and its retreat square no longer guards e6. That is the main practical try against 8...Bf5.

items.prompt: Black to move after 10.Qe2. White threatens a trade on f7. Choose a reply.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Qd6 is the best reply.

hints: Both White pieces aim at e6.
Add a defender and hit the knight.
The queen goes to d6.
items.explain: The queen defends e6 and attacks the knight on e5. White can still trade on f7, and Black keeps the edge afterwards.

items.prompt: White to move. Black played 9...Qc8 instead of 9...Nf6. Is Black still clearly ahead (engine, depth 16)?

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: after 9...Qc8 White is better (at least +40 cp).

hints: Compare with the best reply ...Nf6.
The queen move does not develop a piece.
The engine puts White ahead after this move.
items.explain: The queen move develops nothing and leaves g4 and h5 open for White's queen. Engine, depth 16: White is better. The quiet knight move is the one that holds.
